Subject: MSA redlines — proposed inspection bands & SOC 2 sampling approach (Clarion Health POC)

Hi James / Clarion team,

Following our procurement thread, attaching a consolidated MSA redline and a short SOC2/pen-test sampling proposal for the POC. High-level asks from Clarion we saw: 1) clarity on audit/inspection windows; 2) pen test access and scope; 3) what evidence we can provide versus attestation; and 4) how sampling would look across our SaaS tiers.

Quick summary of what I'm proposing in the attachments:
- Quarterly evidence handoff for SOC 2 artifacts (assertions, control outputs, scoped logs where applicable) with a documented sampling table per product tier.
- Annual pen test window (preferred) with a 10-business-day staging access window; Redwood will provide scoped staging accounts, sanitized logs, and an agreed attack surface matrix. Live production testing requires pre-approval and a narrow scope.
- Sampling bands: Pilot (POC) = 10% sampling, Standard = 25%, Enterprise = 50% for selected control artifacts. We can negotiate higher sampling for SOC 2 Type II reports.

Attachments: Clarion_MSARedline_v3.docx, SOC2_Scope_Sampling.xlsx, pen_test_matrix.pdf

Can you confirm whether Clarion will accept: (a) quarterly evidence bundles + SOC 2 Type II report, and (b) the proposed 10-business-day staging window? If not, please highlight which items are non-starters and we'll route to legal.

If it helps, we can do a 30-min alignment call next week to walk the redlines.

Thanks,
Marcus

Marcus, thanks — appreciate the consolidated materials. A few immediate questions from our side:

1) For the SOC 2 artifacts, our InfoSec team typically requires sampling of logs and config snapshots covering the last 90 days — can Redwood provide (a) time-limited log extracts and (b) a redacted runbook for change control?
2) For the pen test, is the 10-business-day window inclusive of remediation verification? Our procurement/legal prefer a two-phase approach (test + short verification window) so we can close low/med findings quickly.
3) Will Redwood accept a SOC 2 Type II report + signed attestation in lieu of providing raw log exports for certain control families?

I'll copy our security lead on follow up. We can do the alignment call — Friday or early next week works.

- James

Subject: Re: MSA redlines — proposed inspection bands & SOC 2 sampling approach (Clarion Health POC)

Thanks James — quick answers below and a suggested compromise that we hope maps to Clarion's risk appetite.

1) Logs and runbooks: We can provide time-limited log extracts for the 90-day window for scoped environments (staging or a mirrored sampling tenant). For production, due to PII and multi-tenant constraints, we propose redacted extracts and a jointly executed redaction checklist. We'll provide change-control runbook excerpts and a configuration snapshot for the sampled components.

2) Pen test window + remediation verification: Agree with a two-phase approach. Proposal: 10 business days for testing, followed by a 5-business-day verification period for critical/major findings. Redwood will provide remediation evidence for fixed issues and a post-test verification report. We will not permit unauthorised production testing — only the agreed scope in the pen_test_matrix.pdf.

3) SOC 2 Type II + attestation: For certain control families (e.g., logical access, change management) we can accept a SOC 2 Type II report plus a signed attestation if Clarion accepts limited sampling for logs (the sampling bands below). For higher-sensitivity controls we will provide more detailed artifacts.

Suggested sampling bands (POC-oriented):
- POC / Pilot: 10% of sampled artifacts (focus on configuration and authentication logs)
- Standard: 25%
- Enterprise / Regulated: 50%

Next steps:
- I've uploaded a recommended sampling spreadsheet (SOC2_Scope_Sampling.xlsx) and a tracked MSA redline (Clarion_MSARedline_v3.docx) to the Drive link above.
- If Clarion is comfortable, we can convert the MSA to DocuSign for signatures (link in related_links).

If that sounds OK, let's do a 30-min touch on Tue 14th or Thu 16th — happy to take the invite.

Best,
Marcus

James / team,

Thanks for the quick feedback. A couple of legal clarifications from Redwood:

- Pen test scope: we've tightened the language to make explicit that any active testing against production requires prior written approval and will be limited to the agreed attack surface. See Clarion_MSARedline_v3.docx — page 6 (Pen Test Addendum) where I added: "Testing on production systems is only permitted with explicit, documented authorization and under a jointly-agreed plan; unauthorized testing is a material breach."

- Remediation verification: Redwood will provide a remediation verification deliverable within the 5-business-day window. We propose a clause that limits the provider's obligation to commercially reasonable efforts to remediate third-party or customer-driven issues (tracked changes attached).

- Indemnity / limitation: we adjusted indemnity carve-outs to be mutual for security incidents caused by either party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; we left liability caps intact elsewhere.

I've attached a clean tracked-changes doc and a one-page summary of the legal edits: Clarion_MSARedline_v3.docx (tracked) and pen_test_matrix.pdf (operational constraints).

If Clarion legal needs different wording on the remediation verification or the mutual indemnity carve, please highlight specific language and we can iterate quickly.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
